content.rationale: every pointer and keyboard behaviour plus the visual states they drive, with the selected node rendered bolder than the related and hover-neighbour elements; each state change is applied incrementally (stppxysx): interact.ts learns the drawn elements once per graph revision - a node per data-node-id and the visible parts of each data-edge-key, queried at attach and rebuilt only when the graph is swapped - so a later change looks its elements up by the identity it carries instead of scanning the surface; a selection or hover derives the emphasised node and edge sets from the model's incidence index and writes a class only to the elements entering or leaving those sets; and a drag records each pointer position in a pending map and applies it in one relayout per animation frame, the last position of a node winning so nothing is dropped; a lookup that misses ends that change rather than falling back to a scan. Selection emphasis holds its viewport-change bound through to the displayed surface (mntwwzyl): interact.css expresses both highlighting of selected, related and hover-neighbour elements (.is-selected with accent border and 3px outline, [data-node-id].is-related / .is-hover-neighbour with accent border and 2px outline, and .edge.is-related / .is-hover-neighbour with accent stroke) and dimming of unrelated elements (.is-dimmed, .is-dimmed .node__label-secondary, and .edge.is-dimmed variants with resolved text, border and stroke colours mixed in sRGB at 0.3 against --surface) exclusively through passive resolved appearance properties that settle when selection changes, without any per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element opacity or filter stacking surface, compositing group or blend pass; and every viewport change (pan, zoom, pinch, wheel, fit, resize and the recentre a focus move onto a node makes) writes only the single surface transform via applyViewport without walking, querying, re-classing, restyling or refreshing the dimmed or brightened elements, without throttling or dropping viewport updates, and without suppressing emphasis during pan or zoom. A focus move that lands on a node - Tab and Shift and Tab walking the graph order and the interaction's own move to a node - recentres the viewport on it (wzsxvmvw): the centre of the box the layout module draws that node in (qmsmvrnr) is put at the centre of the canvas at the zoom in hand, and what holds that move back is taken per axis - on an axis where the drawn graph fits within the viewport the focused node's centre comes to the centre of the canvas and the margin left at the graph's edge is permitted, the pan limits this viewer records not holding a centring move back there, while on an axis where the drawn graph overflows the viewport the graph keeps covering it and those limits bind, so a node the limits keep off the centre comes to rest on the limit and not beyond it; a fitted axis and an overflowing one are held independently, so one move may centre on one axis while the limit binds on the other; this governs a centring move alone, the clamp recorded for a pan or a zoom being left as it is recorded (yymrxqsk); and the recentre leaves the selection, the emphasis classes and the drawn boxes as they are, writing only the surface transform. The page's declared request to bring a named node into view reaches that same move (ympqvvwr): the controller member the page interface declares for it answers with the recentre a focus arrival on the node it names performs (wzsxvmvw), so the request is the rule's one centring and not a second centring beside it - it moves the pan and leaves the zoom, writes only the surface transform through applyViewport, and, a request to show where a node is being no focus move, leaves the node focus, the selection and the selection reported, the emphasis classes and the drawn boxes as they are. The pointer press and select path (ltrnmrsr) does not reach the recentre, and neither does a change of the panel's own focus nor a focus that ends with no node focused, so a click selects without moving the view. Every position and extent this decision records is one in the frame the surface draws (rtlotqvy): the renderer draws the graph with the layout's bounds origin subtracted (qmsmvrnr), so the interaction maps the canvas to the layout through that origin - the box centre a centring move brings to the centre of the canvas is the centre of the drawn box (wzsxvmvw), the pan and zoom limits hold the drawn graph inside the canvas (yymrxqsk), Fit centres the drawn extent in the canvas (lntrymms), and the pointer's place converted to graph pixels is the layout point the surface draws there (spllzqlw), so a drag keeps its grip on the box it was pressed on; what this decision adds is that mapping at all: the bounds origin, the size the drawn graph spans and the layout's own coordinates are taken as given rather than derived, defaulted or overridden here. A pointer gesture also keeps the subject it was pressed on: at the press interact.ts resolves the node under the pointer once, or records that the press landed on an edge or on empty canvas, and the gesture's later events act on that recorded subject instead of reading their event target, which the browser addresses to the canvas once the press has set pointer capture. A double click therefore asks the editor for the document of the node its gesture was pressed on, a second double click on another node asks for that node and not the first, and a double click on empty canvas asks for no node's document; a press that becomes a drag, a pan or a pinch fixes no double-click subject, and a double click delivered with no gesture behind it still resolves from the element it is addressed to.
